scope: Second R3 gate batch on HEAD: Pause/Resume/resize, Reset, Close, request->ready and GPU render. The instrument is the repository's own PD5 scripted host timing probe compiled into cuexis_execution_device_probe, so the renderer is the real OpenGL backend rather than the CPU test renderer. Diagnostic/test-only: it decides only the gates it measures, and D2/D3/Snapshot/queue are recorded as undecided because no comparable non-intrusive boundary exists.

source.head: 6256af8b7d349b14a6d5b006d7632711152e96fa
source.why_this_instrument: tests/pd/pd5_device_probe.cpp defines CUEXIS_PD5_DEVICE and includes pd5_host_probe.cpp, so the same scripted host harness runs against OpenGlBackend with the GPU timer query enabled; the plain cuexis_pd_host_probe target compiles the CPU TestPresentationRenderer instead and cannot produce gpu_render at all.

groups.per_cycle_operations: pause, resume, pause, reset_paused (close+reload+pause), resume, reset_running (close+reload), resize 960x540/1280x720 alternating
groups.boundary: the probe's control() lambda records start before the command, confirmed after the host call returns, and end after the next frame's present returns, so each reading is command -> state confirmed -> usable frame presented
groups.statistics: the plan fixes controls to the max of every pre-declared operation in the window, not a percentile; 3 fresh processes x 20 cycles = 60 readings per control metric, and the reported value is the maximum
validity: exit code 0 (the probe's own assertions on receipt status, storage live count and Replay equivalence must hold)
each control metric has exactly 20 readings per process and close exactly 1
the probe prints PD5_ID with mode=controls and gpu_timer=true

groups.workload: CUEXIS_PD5_MODE=stream, CUEXIS_PD5_FRAMES=1200, CUEXIS_PD5_WARMUP=64, CUEXIS_PD5_RATE=240, CUEXIS_PD5_GPU_TIMER=1, CUEXIS_PD5_SMOKE=1
groups.boundary: request_to_ready covers clock poll -> host->advance -> host->sample returning the frame the caller can use; gpu_render is the timer-query interval around the backend's GPU command range. present_call and request_to_present_return are reported separately and are never substituted for either gate.
groups.statistics: per-process p99 over 1200 samples (the plan requires n>=1000 for a p99); three fresh processes, gate passes only if every process passes
validity: request_to_ready, gpu_render, cpu_submit, present_call and request_to_present_return each have exactly 1200 readings per process
every advance returns Executed at the requested horizon (the probe asserts this per frame)

groups.reason: no instrument exposes a comparable non-intrusive boundary for these four stages on this source. The plan says that when such a boundary is missing the budget is recorded as undecided and that probe timestamps cannot be accepted in its place; PD-5 reached the same conclusion, so this batch does not invent one.

out_of_scope: applicable Seek: still undecided. The functional matrix runs the CPU test renderer at 33/129 records and stamps formal:false, and the device probe's host harness has no seek scenario, so no reading here is the 20 ms gate.
initial load: measured in the first batch and not repeated.
relative read: measured in the first batch and not repeated.
shared_rules: no re-sampling and no retries to pass
a pilot run with 8-16 frames was used only to confirm the instrument emits gpu_render; it is not part of any group
machine left otherwise idle during both groups
no threshold, scope or scenario is modified by this batch

amendments.what: The first attempt completed its first process but the driver crashed while computing statistics, because the local statistics() helper shadowed the imported statistics module. No reading was printed or recorded; the process log is preserved as controls.aborted-1/run-00.log.txt and is not used. The fix renames the import alias; the group was then run as registered with three fresh processes.
